analysis: The PR only changes documentation: docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head lines 2876-3299 and surrounding ranges) and docs/provider/sandboxes.md. No executable code, keys, protocol handling or controls change. Examined for threat-model impact: the sandbox page (head patch hunks around lines 21-43, 155-166) now documents a `darkbloom waitlist sandbox` step and says `sandbox setup` installs nothing until the account is approved. This touches TB-013 / A-019 / T-061 (CLI downloads and runs the add-on installer as the Mac owner). It adds an account-level approval gate before the installer runs and sends nothing about the Mac. That reduces rather than adds exposure, but only if the CLI actually implements it. The new command, waitlist request and error strings (for example 'Could not reach the Darkbloom Sandbox waitlist') are not in supplied evidence. Nothing in the supplied evidence shows a regression such as skipping the installer's verification step. The `darkbloom waitlist` command, its request and its auth handling (A-008 provider token reuse) are in separate files not supplied here. A reviewer of the Swift code should check that the waitlist request goes only to the intended sandbox/coordinator host with the account token, and that a failed or unreachable check really fails closed. The troubleshooting text says it does ('checked and installed nothing'). The cli-reference.md head excerpts I saw (paths table, provider.toml keys, env passthrough, cluster docs) appear to be unchanged context. I could not see the changed ranges at head lines 1360-1385 or 1635-1724; the patch excerpt is truncated, so the new waitlist reference section was not reviewed. No finding is raised. Deeper review is recommended only to verify that the documented waitlist and setup gating match the implementation, since the docs claim behavior that cannot be confirmed from this evidence.
